A ChatGPT Business Agent can explain your returns policy, but your service team handles what it gets wrong.

OpenAI has opened Business Agents to ecommerce and online service businesses outside the US. In this clip Hannah sets out what an agent does. It explains products and policies and sends people to your site. It can't take a purchase, make a booking or check an order.

So every answer about delivery or returns has to match your website exactly. If the agent says thirty days and the site says fourteen, the customer brings that to you, not to OpenAI.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

clips.text: What can the agent actually do for a customer? Explain products and policies, and send people to your website. That's the boundary. It can't complete a purchase, make a booking or check an order. The buying still happens on your site. Which means every answer it gives about delivery or returns has to match the website exactly. If the agent says thirty days and the site says fourteen, the customer brings that to your service team, not to OpenAI.

youtube.title: Two AI prompts for setting up a ChatGPT Business Agent
youtube.description:
James and Hannah set out two jobs to hand to AI when you build a ChatGPT Business Agent. One drafts the agent's instructions from your own product, delivery and returns pages. The other checks the agent's answers to your most common customer questions against your website.

clips.linkedin:
Hand AI your ChatGPT agent's answers to your top twenty customer questions and it checks each against your website.

Brands outside the US can now build a Business Agent in ChatGPT. Most of the setup is a person signing verification forms, but Hannah and I picked out two jobs that suit AI well.

The first is the agent's brief. Give AI your live product, delivery and returns pages and it drafts the agent's instructions, with each claim tied to its source page and a list of where your pages contradict each other. A person still signs it off.

The second is the test. Give it the twenty questions your service inbox gets most and the agent's preview answers, and it marks each one right, wrong or unclear, with a fix. Run it again whenever your delivery or returns terms change.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. Both prompts are in the show notes.

Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/chatgpt-business-agents-outside-us-uk-brands/
clips.text: Most of the setup is a person signing forms, but two jobs suit AI well. The first is writing the agent's brief from pages you already stand behind. Give it your live product, delivery and returns pages, and it hands back a draft set of agent instructions, with every claim tied to the page it came from and a list of anything the pages contradict. A person still signs it off, ideally whoever approves your ad copy. The second is the test before you publish. Give it the twenty questions your service inbox gets most, plus the agent's answers from the preview, and it marks each answer against your website as right, wrong or unclear, with the fix. Run it again whenever your returns or delivery terms change. The prompts are in the show notes.
